decisions.reason: The margin analysis builds on the firm's established data offer and has its own page, so it is a visible commitment that management would keep while early results can still be attributed to the launch phase.
The gas tariff comparison sits close to the core market-data business and is publicly presented, so dropping it would write off sunk data investments and require justifying the decision.
The electricity tariff calculator is a core-adjacent offer with its own page and fits the central platform direction the firm has announced, so management persists with it.

The energy tariff calculator is only mentioned on the website, so the public commitment is low, but it builds on shared tariff databases and can still be integrated into the platform, so it is kept for now.
The area definition tool has its own page and supports the regional tariff and margin tools, which raises its sunk value and its strategic justification within the platform.

The site-specific comparison is only mentioned and overlaps with products B and C, so it is the likeliest drop candidate, but its low marginal cost on existing data infrastructure makes keeping it the default.
